params.write_excel: Whether to output the Excel report

params.feature_cols: Raw model input features; when empty, numeric columns are selected automatically, excluding target/split/oot/weight
params.weight_col: Sample-weight field; passed to GBM training, param_search, and evaluation
params.extra_eval_datasets: Dict of extra evaluation datasets; keys must not conflict with ins/oos/oot

level2.name: Existing Split Fields

params.split_col: Recommended split field; supports ins/oos/oot, highest priority
params.sample_col: Compatible legacy split field, default sample_ind
params.oot_col: OOT flag field; used when there is no split/sample field

rules: split_col takes precedence over sample_col
split_col must contain non-empty ins and oos; since 0.7.0, no OOT is synthesized by default when a real oot is missing, and an OOS copy is used only with an explicit synthesize_missing_oot=true
When there is no split/sample, OOT is split off first with oot_col, and INS/OOS are then split with split_config

split_config.random_state: Split random seed; when empty, inherits the top-level random_state

feature_selection.corr_max_iterations: Maximum number of iteration rounds for correlation screening
feature_selection.corr_block_size: Feature-column block size of the weighted correlation matrix, default 256

level2.name: Reuse of Screening Artifacts

params.feature_validation_result: After passing a FeatureValidationPipelineResult, it is converted into a screening artifact
params.feature_selection_mode: run/from_artifact/skip; controls whether to re-screen, reuse the artifact, or skip screening
params.reuse_screening_woe: Whether to reuse the WOE artifact in the screening artifact

rules: screening_artifact takes precedence over feature_validation_result
from_artifact depends on an existing screening artifact
skip bypasses screening and uses feature_cols directly

level2.name: WOE Engine Reuse from the Screening Stage (G00)

params.screening_artifact: FVP/standalone screening artifact; the monotone engine self-fitted by screening is attached with the artifact, and the CM-side _reuse_screening_woe reuses it directly without refitting (WOE_Master attaches only the table + a warning)

params.woe_fit_query: Filter condition applied to the INS sample before the WOE fit

woe_params.sv_min_bin_size: 0.8.0 SV bin share threshold [0.0,1.0), default 0.0 = off
woe_params.sv_small_policy: 0.8.0 keep (default)/neutral/merge_missing, fallback for sub-threshold SV bins
woe_params.sv_woe_smoothing: 0.8.0 none (default)/laplace, bad-rate shrinkage of SV bin WOE

monotone_woe_params.sv_min_bin_size: 0.8.0 SV bin share threshold [0.0,1.0), default 0.0 = off
monotone_woe_params.sv_small_policy: 0.8.0 keep (default)/neutral/merge_missing, fallback for sub-threshold SV bins
monotone_woe_params.sv_woe_smoothing: 0.8.0 none (default)/laplace, bad-rate shrinkage of SV bin WOE
monotone_woe_params.unseen_special_policy: 0.8.2 normal_bin (default)/neutral; numeric special values declared but absent from the fit sample: binned as ordinary values / a placeholder bin takes missing_woe

level2.name: WOE and Model Feature Source

params.gbm_feature_source: woe/raw, or a dict configured per model; LR always uses WOE

rules: By default all models use WOE features, keeping the old behavior
With gbm_feature_source='raw', lgb/xgb/cat use raw features
dict keys may only be lgb/xgb/cat, and values may only be raw/woe
raw mode does no automatic categorical encoding

params.train_models: List of models to train, default lr/lgb/xgb/cat

level2.name: LR Parameter Search

params.lr_search_enabled: Whether to run grid_search_params for LR
params.lr_search_params: Extra parameter overrides for the LR search
params.use_lr_search_params: Whether to merge the found best_params into the final LR training

rules: Runs only when train_models contains lr and lr_search_enabled=true
The search runs on WOE features

level2.name: GBM warm-start

params.warm_start_models: Models to apply warm-start to, default lgb/xgb
params.warm_start_on_unsupported: skip or raise when an unsupported model is encountered
params.warm_start_apply_to_optuna: Whether warm-start takes part in the GBM optuna refit/search

rules: warm_start_score_col must be provided when warm_start_enabled=true
Currently only lgb/xgb are supported; cat is skipped by default
probability is clipped first and then converted to log_odds

params.lr_elimination_mode: None (off by default) or "pvalue": after fitting, remove features one by one by coefficient p-value and refit
params.lr_elimination_params: pvalue_threshold=0.05 / min_features=1 / max_iterations=20 / tie_breaker="pvalue"; the trace goes to feature_selection_summary['lr_elimination'] and lr_pvalue_elimination.csv

optional.level1: OOT Governance (Leakage Prevention in the Candidate Stage)

level2.name: OOT governance

params.candidate_mode: One-switch candidate-mode tightening: forbid OOT (forbidden_splits gets oot merged in), do not synthesize OOT, evaluate only ins/oos, search uses only oos, and backward does not read OOT; conflicts with explicitly opposite configuration raise an error directly
params.synthesize_missing_oot: Whether to substitute an OOS copy when OOT is missing; default false since 0.7.0, so splits contain no oot and all downstream steps skip automatically; only an explicit true synthesizes it and issues a UserWarning
params.evaluation_splits: Evaluation split allowlist; default [ins, oos] since 0.7.0, so perf/plots/Excel do not consume OOT by default (extra_eval_datasets is not restricted); an explicit list can override it
params.forbidden_splits: Hard gate: raises ValueError whenever any component (search/backward/evaluation, including ones brought in through optuna_params/backward_params) is about to consume a forbidden split
params.search_eval_splits: Source of eval_sets for LR search and Optuna; default [oos] since 0.7.0, so OOT is not used for candidate tuning by default; an explicit list is strictly checked for existence
params.search_objective_when_no_oot: Fallback objective when the search eval sets do not include oot and no objective is set explicitly, default max_primary
params.backward_validation_split: Validation source for backward, default oos
params.backward_report_splits: Source of backward test_data_dict; default [] since 0.7.0, to keep the per-round report from reading OOT; an explicit list can override it

rules: The run artifacts (Result.split_governance and the model metadata) record candidate_mode/oot_synthesized/oot_withheld, so that acceptance can tell whether the OOT is real
Under candidate_mode, a real OOT in the data is split off but never consumed throughout (oot_withheld=true)

optional.level1: Evaluation Governance (Multi-Label / Special Scores / Direction / Weights)

level2.name: Evaluation governance

params.eval_target_cols: List of extra evaluation labels; the effective label set = [target_col] + eval_target_cols, de-duplicated. The same model scores are computed only once and reused for all labels; the perf tables are stacked vertically with a new tgt_name column (when not set, the output structure is exactly the same as the old version)
params.all_missing_score_value: Score override value (e.g. -1) for rows where all raw model input features are missing; the criterion is exactly the same as Core.scoring's all_missing_spec_value, and it is written into the model artifact metadata together with the raw feature list used for the criterion; on the production side, Core.scoring(all_missing_spec_value=metadata value) is enough to align
params.special_score_values: Special scores (e.g. [-1]) form their own evaluation bin: they take no part in the quantile boundaries, the gains table gives them a separate row, and ranking metrics such as AUC/KS/avgScore are based on the non-special rows; unweighted/weighted use the same basis
params.gains_ascending: Default true since 0.7.0: summary, Gains, weighted Gains, and evaluation plots uniformly use ascending score order (bin 1 = low score, low risk); an explicit false keeps the descending basis
params.eval_weight_col: Weight column for the evaluation stage: inherit (default) = reuse weight_col; null = unweighted evaluation (training weights no longer implicitly affect evaluation, and the eval weights of search/backward are kept in step); another string = explicitly specify the evaluation weight column

rules: All evaluation labels must exist in the input data and in every extra_eval_datasets frame
When all_missing_score_value is used together with special_score_values, rows overridden with -1 automatically fall into the separate special bin
gains_ascending controls the direction of both the tables and the evaluate_performance distribution plots, avoiding basis drift between the charts of the same run

level2.name: Backward

params.backward_enabled: Whether to run backward feature selection
params.backward_model: Model used for stepwise regression, default lgb
params.use_backward_features: Whether the final model uses the features selected by backward

rules: backward runs on WOE features by default
In GBM raw mode with use_backward_features=true, the selected _woe features are mapped back to the raw columns

params.optuna_models: GBM models to run Optuna on, default lgb/xgb/cat
params.optuna_params: Override parameters such as Optuna search_spaces/common/fit_kwargs

params.explain_models: List of models to run explainability such as SHAP/LIME/PDP on
params.owen_enabled: Whether to run the Owen coalition explanation

params.perf_pct_bins: Number of bins for performance evaluation
params.perf_min_bin_prop: Minimum bin share for performance evaluation

params.save_models: Whether to save the model pkl and WOE artifacts
params.model_output_dir: Model output directory; when empty, output_dir/models is used
params.model_include_metadata: Whether to save the metadata envelope
params.save_woe_artifacts: Whether to save artifacts such as the WOE table/engine

sv_min_bin_size.meaning: 0.8.0 SV bin share threshold; prop = n_bin / N_total (no eps added to the denominator), and the fallback triggers only when strictly below this value; 0.0 = off

sv_small_policy.meaning: 0.8.0 fallback for sub-threshold SV bins: keep = old behavior; neutral = WOE/IV set to 0; merge_missing = counts merged into the [Missing] bin and recomputed, the stored WOE of merged rows is rewritten to the [Missing] WOE with IV set to 0, and when there is no [Missing] bin it degrades to neutral with a warning

sv_woe_smoothing.meaning: 0.8.0 SV bin WOE smoothing; laplace uses bad-rate shrinkage r=(n_bad+α·p)/(n_bin+α) and then converts back to shares, applying only to SV bins and leaving ordinary bins untouched

sv_smoothing_alpha.meaning: 0.8.0 smoothing strength α; 0.0 is bit-for-bit equivalent to the old empirical WOE, and as α→∞ the WOE shrinks monotonically to 0, with stronger shrinkage the fewer samples a bin has

missing_woe.meaning: WOE for NaN not declared as special_values

special_values.meaning: Special values that need their own bin

cate_feats.meaning: Categorical features; the Pipeline maps them from categorical_features

bin_label_decimals.meaning: Number of decimal places shown for bin boundaries

monotone_woe_params.pipeline_note: CreditModelPipeline currently passes monotone_woe_params directly to the MonotoneWOEBinner constructor, and explicitly reads only chi2_binning to pass to fit; fit-only keys other than the default constructor parameters need care. The fit-only pop list is {chi2_binning, chi2_p, chi2_init_size, n_jobs}; the four sv_* keys are constructor parameters and are not on that list, so they correctly enter __init__; never add sv_* to the fit-only list, otherwise a TypeError will be raised.
